title: Stoichiometry
content: Stoichiometry is a part of chemistry which deals with the quantities of substances taking part in a chemical reaction.
e: Stoichiometry is a part of chemistry which deals with the quantities of substances taking part in a chemical reaction. Stoichiometry is the quantitative bookkeeping of how much of each substance takes part in a reaction. Stoichiometry is the word this version is asking about.

title: Law of Conservation of Mass
content: Law of Conservation of Mass states that the total mass of reactant(s) is equal to the total mass of the product(s).
e: Law of Conservation of Mass states that the total mass of reactant(s) is equal to the total mass of the product(s). Mass is conserved in a chemical change: the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products. Law of Conservation of Mass is the word this version is asking about.

title: Limiting reactant
content: Limiting reactant is the reactant in a chemical reaction that limits the amount of product because the reaction stops when the limiting reactant is completely consumed.
e: Limiting reactant is the reactant in a chemical reaction that limits the amount of product because the reaction stops when the limiting reactant is completely consumed. The limiting reactant is the one that is used up first and therefore caps how much product can form. Limiting reactant is the word this version is asking about.

title: Molarity
content: The molarity (M) of a solution is the quantity in moles of the solute dissolved in one cubic decimetre of the solution.
e: The molarity (M) of a solution is the quantity in moles of the solute dissolved in one cubic decimetre of the solution. The SI base unit of length is the metre, symbol m. Molarity is moles of solute per cubic decimetre of solution.

title: Titration
content: Titration is the procedure in which a solution of a standard reagent (reactant) is added to a specific volume of a solution of unknown molarity.
e: Titration is the procedure in which a solution of a standard reagent (reactant) is added to a specific volume of a solution of unknown molarity. Titration adds a standard solution of known concentration until the reaction with an unknown is complete. Molarity is moles of solute per cubic decimetre of solution.
